steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C).
Combine 3 tablespoons softened butter, brown sugar, and ¼ teaspoon cinnamon in a small bowl; spread over 1 side each bread slice. Place bread slices, buttered-sides up, on a baking sheet.
Bake in the preheated oven until bread is crisp and topping is bubbly, 8 to 10 minutes. Cut each bread slice into 8 small triangles or squares. Set croutons aside.
Melt 2 tablespoons butter in a medium saucepan. Add onion; cook until tender. Stir in 1 can broth; bring to a boil. Cover, reduce heat, and simmer for 15 minutes.

Fill blender or the bowl of a food processor halfway with broth mixture. Cover and hold lid down with a potholder; pulse a few times before leaving on to blend. Pour into a saucepan. Repeat with remaining broth mixture.

Stir remaining 1 can broth, pumpkin purée, salt, ¼ teaspoon cinnamon, ginger, and black pepper into puréed broth mixture; bring to a boil. Cover, reduce heat, and simmer 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in cream and heat through; do not boil. Divide soup among serving bowls; top with croutons.

raw_recipe.headline: Cream of Pumpkin Soup
raw_recipe.description: This comforting cream of pumpkin soup recipe, made with chicken broth, pumpkin purée, and warm spices, is garnished with whole-wheat cinnamon croutons.

review.reviewBody: Great soup on a cold day! I made it lowfat by using Pam instead of butter, and using skim milk thickened with corn starch instead of whipping cream. Also, instead of croutons, I just floated some sliced scallions on the top to make it pretty. Thanks for the recipe!

We loved this soup. I made a few modifications but it turned out great. I roasted and puréed 2 small pumpkins. I added 6 whole cloves with the onions and sautéed then continued the simmer with the cloves for 15 minutes. Then removed the cloves. I increased the cinnamon to 1/2 tsp. I made croutons by melting 1 Tbs butter and 1 Tbs olive oil in a pan and tossed in cubed sourdough bread. I pan roasted until crispy and golden. It was delicious!

Yes, I made adjustments; but had I not read this great recipe, I could not have modified it! I omitted the croutons. Cooked the chopped onion in butter, added the chicken broth, pureed with an immersion blender, added 1/4 cup brown sugar, 1 tsp pumpkin pie spice, 1 tsp creole seasoning and 1/4 tsp cayenne. Added two 15 oz cans of pumpkin puree, blended with immersion blender and heated through; added 1 cup heavy whipping cream, blended with immersion blender. Top with sliced green onions and crumbled bacon. (Hint: Store cooked bacon in a baggie in freezer - handy to pull out a couple of strips at a time, crumble, heat in microwave and sprinkle on top of yummy pumpkin soup with sliced green onions.)

Easier than butternut squash soup. After simmering 1/2 an onion and broth, I added 1/2 the second can of broth to cool it a bit then used the hand blender in the pot. Added the rest of the broth, and as others suggested, added 1/4 cup brown sugar, 1/2 tsp cinnamon, 1/4 tsp ginger, 1/8 tsp cayenne and cut salt down to just a pinch since I used regular chicken broth. Could still use more spices. Changed cream to 1/2 cup milk and 1/2 cup half and half. Will make again.

We doubled spices and added a small amount of brown sugar to taste. 1/8 tsp Cayenne pepper.

The croutons make this awesome. 

Don' t puree the onion / soup while it is HOT it will EXPLODE. wait for it to cool down. 

 we added a can of pureed Campbell's hearty chicken soup after we lost half our onions & chicken soup in the explosion. LOL..

Very good soup! I also used less nutmeg (3/4tsp) and 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp garlic seasoning and 2 vegetable bouillon cubes. I cooked the onion and carrots in the pot with oil until tender and then added the water, cubed pumpkin and potatoes and cooked until done. Added seasonings and simmered for 1 hr. 
I used Greek yogurt instead of the cream before serving and it tasted yummy!

I have been making this fabulous recipe for 2 years now and it is an absolute hit! I skip the crouton and just make the soup. I double the onion serving and only blend half, the other half I add it directly to the soup once blended. It gives and extra little crunch and so much flavor. I use the concentrated chicken broth and diluted in water instead of actualy chicken broth. I will adjust cinnamon and ginger to taste and sometimes add extra chicken broth (not diluted). We like it salty. It is unfortunate others finds the taste blend for them because here it is full of flavor! Not all taste buds are the same and it is the adjuments that makes it fantastic for your household.

Agree with others it was a bit bland as written. 2nd go, sauted onions, garlic and chopped up bacon. Declare with basalmic vinegar, add rest of ingredients plus Wyler chx bouillon powder and garlic powder. Turned out great. In leu of sweet croutons, I tossed in olive oil, salt, pepper, Tyler's and garlic powder. Tuned out to be a great meal served with salad.

I'm giving this five stars, but its not a solid five as I JUST took it off the stove and won't be eating it until tomorrow. I also increased the spices and added 3 heaping teaspoons of brown sugar to the soup. Instead of whipping cream, I put in a quarter package of reduced fat cream cheese and let it melt in the soup, and maybe 1/2 cup of skim milk since that's all I have. I couldn't stop sampling it when I took it off the stove, so I know it'll be good. As someone suggested, I also used cinnamon bread, but I cut that into cubes, tossed them in melted butter, put them in a baking dish, sprinkled apple pie spices over them and baked them into croutons. I keep eating those too, so I think its going to be a good meal!

After the 1st time making it, the 2nd time I made a bunch of changes & it came out soooo yummy - reminded me of Thai food! For the soup base: omitted the onion & broth, simmered the pumpkin with 1/2 cup of brown sugar, dbl all the spices plus adding 1/4 tsp of cayenne & nutmeg. Tasted as I spiced it up & lastly added whipping cream & then stored in fridge for 2 days. Day of serving: softened 3 very small onions, then added broth, chopped 1/2 red bell pepper & 1 small yam covered until cooked, then cooked chicken tenders & chopped after cooked thru. Once everything was cooked through I added the pumpkin base. Delicious over rice too.
I added 1/8 teaspoon cayenne pepper, and 2 cans pumpkin puree.
Bland and inedible
I followed the recipe exactly and the product was inedible. As others have said, it was watery, very little taste, and even had a bit of a bitter taste to it. We did not eat any of it.
Followed the recipe to a T. Family was not crazy about it. I didn't find any pumpkin flavor to it.
This was delicious!!! I found some pumpkin shaped pasta that my kids were excited about, so I boiled those and then added them into the soup. I would absolutely make this again!
I made this twice. First time it came a little thicker, which I loved. The soup is delicious and the croutons make it.
Fantastic soup!
Delicious! I didn't make the croutons, since I don't like bread. I used veggie broth instead of chicken broth, and used lactose free heavy cream.
I made the soup and we loved it!

This is WAY TO BLAND and I even doubled the spies. It tastes like warmed up canned pumpking puree with cream and chicken broth, which it pretty much is. I doubt I will make this again, but if I did I would put lots more onion in and maybe an apple or two.
